title: Bounded-below cohomology comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a ring, and $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$
the comparison morphism. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)$ the unit of the
adjunction between
$\nu_X^*:D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)\to D^+(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ and
$R\nu_{X,*}$ is an isomorphism

$$
K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\nu_{X,*}\nu_X^*K\quad\text{in }D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda).
$$

Consequently $\nu_X^*:D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)\to D^+(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is
fully faithful, and there is a canonical isomorphism in the derived category
of $\Lambda$-modules

$$
R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\nu_X^*K)\simeq R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{ét}},K).
$$

More generally, for a pro-étale affine $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ with $U_i$
affine and étale over $X$,

$$
R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proét}},(\nu_X^*K)|_U)\simeq
\varinjlim_iR\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K|_{U_i}).
$$

The colimit here is a filtered derived colimit, so its cohomology is the
filtered colimit of the cohomology groups.

Coefficients are discrete, and modules are left modules. Thus module sheaves mean sheaves of left $\Lambda$-modules, equivalently modules over the constant ring sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], in a common larger universe in which the underlying site categories are small. The small sites and comparison geometric morphism are those of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with its set inverse image applied to addition and every scalar action for any ring $\Lambda$. Derived categories are the localizations at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; $D^+$ means cohomology vanishes sufficiently far below [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. The right derived functors of comparison direct image and sections at the terminal object use [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. A pro-étale affine is as in [sk-def-pe-morphisms]; the presentation above is indexed by a nonempty small cofiltered category, and the colimit is over its opposite filtered category.

proof.text: Put $L=\nu_X^*$ and $R=\nu_{X,*}$ on left $\Lambda$-module sheaves. The geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] acts on addition and each scalar endomorphism; finite-product preservation gives addition on inverse images, and each scalar action is carried over separately. The unit and counit respect addition and every scalar action by naturality; thus both directions of the Hom transpose preserve module homomorphisms. This restricts the set adjunction to a module adjunction for any ring. For morphisms $f,g$, finite-product preservation identifies $L(f+g)=L(+)(Lf,Lg)\Delta$ with $Lf+Lg$, and sends zero to zero; $R$ preserves sums and zero by its sectionwise restriction formula. Thus both functors are additive. Module-sheaf kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The underlying inverse image preserves finite limits, hence $L$ preserves kernels; its module left-adjoint property gives preservation of cokernels. Thus $L$ is exact. $R$ is additive and left exact, since the Hom adjunction transports the universal property of kernels. The general coefficient unit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-grothendieck-unit] explicitly includes left modules over any ring and makes $F\to RLF$ invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], termwise $L$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and $D^+$.

Choose a representative $C$ of $K$ and a cohomology lower bound $a$. Replace it by the good truncation zero below $a$, with degree $a$ term $\operatorname{coker}d_C^{a-1}$. The quotient map in degree $a$, the identity above $a$ and zero below $a$ define a morphism of complexes from $C$ to this truncation. The kernel of the truncation differential out of degree $a$ is $\ker d_C^a/\operatorname{im}d_C^{a-1}=H^a(C)$, and higher cohomology is unchanged. Below $a$ both cohomologies vanish by the choice of $a$, so this replacement is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] on either small ringed site to choose bounded-below termwise-injective K-injective resolutions; in particular choose $I$ representing $K$, so $LI$ represents $LK$. These module categories have enough injectives: resolve $F[0]$ this way, and starting at the lowest degree below zero split off its injective term and the next term as a contractible pair. Each such monomorphism splits by injectivity, and a direct summand of an injective is injective by extending into the larger object and projecting. After finitely many removals $F$ embeds into the remaining injective degree-zero term. Sections at the terminal object are additive and left exact, since addition and kernels are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] constructs the bounded-below right derived functor $\mathbf R R$ and both derived section functors, computed on these resolutions. Neither cited statement restricts the ring to be finite.

Construct the actual derived adjunction. For arbitrary objects of the two $D^+$ categories, choose bounded-below representing complexes $M$ on the étale site and $N$ on the pro-étale site as in step 2, and resolve $N\to J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], $RJ$ is K-injective since $L$ is exact. The localization bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], termwise adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], and injective calculation [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+}(LM,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K^+}(LM,J)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{K^+}(M,RJ)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^+}(M,\mathbf R R N).$$
The identity of $LM$, represented by a resolution $j:LM\to J$, transposes to $Rj\circ\eta_M$. Hence the derived unit is precisely represented by $M\to RLM\to RJ$.

source.place: 08BJ (lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives) and 070I (lemma-K-injective); the Hom-adjunction argument is written out here on D^+, rather than assuming an unbounded derived adjunction

proof.text: Each $LI^r$ is $R$-acyclic by [lem-pe-comparison-injective-left-modules-acyclic], explicitly stated for arbitrary, possibly noncommutative $\Lambda$. Resolve $LI\xrightarrow{j}J$ by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. The terms of $J$ are $R$-acyclic by clause 1 of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity-quasi-iso], with a common lower bound, makes $Rj:RLI\to RJ$ a quasi-isomorphism. The unit $I\to RLI$ is termwise invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-grothendieck-unit]; naturality gives $RL(d_I^r)\eta_{I^r}=\eta_{I^{r+1}}d_I^r$, hence $d_I^r\eta_{I^r}^{-1}=\eta_{I^{r+1}}^{-1}RL(d_I^r)$. Thus the inverse components also form a chain map. Step 3 therefore represents the derived unit at $K$ by a composite of quasi-isomorphisms. This proves the claimed natural unit isomorphism.

proof.text: The derived adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(LK,LH)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,\mathbf R R LH)$. It sends $L(f)$ to $\mathbf R R(Lf)\eta_K=\eta_H f$. Composition with the invertible $\eta_H$ is a bijection, so the actual map $f\mapsto L(f)$ is bijective. This is full faithfulness.

For an arbitrary object of $D^+(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ choose a bounded-below representing complex $N$ and a bounded-below injective resolution $N\to J$ [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. $R$ preserves injectives: a map $A\to RJ^r$ transposes to $LA\to J^r$, extends along $LA\hookrightarrow LB$ for a monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$ by exactness of $L$, and transposes back to $B\to RJ^r$. Hence $RJ$ is termwise injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], derived sections of $\mathbf R R N$ are represented by $\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{ét}},RJ)$, while those of $N$ are represented by $\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proét}},J)$. These are the same complex: [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] defines $R$ as restriction, and the inclusion sends the terminal object $X$ to $X$. The equality commutes with differentials and morphisms of complexes. Morphisms in the derived category between the chosen resolutions are represented uniquely up to homotopy by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; applying the equal section complexes to those representatives therefore gives the canonical natural derived-sections comparison. For $N=LK$, compose it with derived sections of the unit in step 4, then invert, to obtain the displayed orientation of global sections.

source.place: 099W (lemma-compare-cohomology), computed at the terminal object on injective resolutions

proof.text: Apply the existing detailed input [det-sf-comparison-affine-continuity] to the same scheme $X$, arbitrary ring $\Lambda$, bounded-below $K$, and small cofiltered affine étale presentation of $U$. Its statement gives the two canonical cohomology isomorphisms and their equivalent filtered-derived-colimit formula, for exactly $(\nu_X^*K)|_U$. The transition maps are affine: for a map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by $\varphi:A\to B$, the inverse image of every principal open $D(f)$ is the affine $D(\varphi(f))=\operatorname{Spec}B_{\varphi(f)}$. This uses the existing arbitrary-ring statement, rather than the older finite-coefficient continuity theorem outside its hypotheses. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] gives exact filtered colimits of left modules over any ring. Exactness applied to kernels, images and quotients yields $H^n(\varinjlim C_i)=\varinjlim H^n(C_i)$; termwise filtered colimit therefore computes the derived colimit and its claimed cohomology.

Ensures R sends K-injectives to K-injectives once L is proved exact; used only to construct the bounded-below Hom adjunction.

Its exact filtered-colimit clause identifies the cohomology of the derived colimit with the filtered colimit of cohomology modules.

lean.note: All clauses: derived unit, full faithfulness and canonical global comparison in boundedBelowComparison; affine derived-colimit and every-degree cohomology formulas in affineBoundedBelowComparison. The latter uses arbitrary bounded-below injective representatives and the actual unit/resolution/restriction cocone; Q of the termwise filtered colimit represents the derived colimit since filtered module colimits are exact. Coefficients are arbitrary rings, with no finiteness or commutativity restriction.
